detail:
NIAMS describes Sjögren's disease, also called Sjögren's syndrome, as a chronic autoimmune disorder in which the immune system attacks the glands that make moisture in the eyes, mouth, and other parts of the body. It predominantly affects women, can start at any age, and can occur by itself or alongside other autoimmune conditions such as rheumatoid arthritis or lupus.

NIAMS lists the main symptoms as dry eyes, which can burn, itch, or feel sandy, and dry mouth, which can make swallowing, speaking, and tasting harder and raises the risk of dental decay and mouth infections. Many people also report fatigue and joint and muscle pain, and the disease can affect the lungs, kidneys, and nervous system. There is no single test: evaluation can include measuring tear and saliva production, blood tests for certain antibodies, and sometimes a salivary gland biopsy.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about evaluation for Sjögren's symptoms.
sourceName: National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases
sourceVideoTitle: Sjogren's Disease Symptoms - Dry Mouth & Eyes | NIAMS
summary: NIAMS gives an overview of Sjögren's disease, a chronic autoimmune disorder in which the immune system attacks moisture-producing glands, covering its symptoms, causes, and how it is recognized.
takeaways: sjögren's mainly attacks glands that make tears and saliva
dry eyes and dry mouth are the hallmark symptoms sources describe
fatigue and joint and muscle pain are also commonly reported
there is no single test; diagnosis combines exams, labs, and gland tests
title: Sjögren's syndrome: dryness from an immune attack on glands
